chapter: Coming up in New York and Harlem theatres
title: Meeting Duke Ellington in 1922 and his rise to the Cotton Club
summary: Whaley meets Duke at Robinson's Restaurant, tells how Duke took over Elmer Snowden's band from Sonny Greer, and describes Hardwick, Carney and Bubber Miley.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: And after that, Duke come along, when I met Duke it was at the Robinson Restaurant. Did I tell you that before.
I was sitting down in Robinson's
Restaurant and they had a piano in there, see.
That's Duke Ellington you're talking about. What year was that, Tom.

That was in 1922 and I was sitting down there playing the piano and somebody says there's Duke Ellington, well, I had heard about him but I didn't know him so I kept on playing and he come over, and they introduced me to him. He was down at the Kit Kat -- no, what is that club downtown.
Let me see, there were so many, I can't remember -- it's kind of hard for me to remember 1922, I was 12 then.
It was -- anyway it's a club --
It might have been the Kit Kat.
No, not the Kit Kat, it was some other club and this guy Sonny Greer and the guitar player had the band.

Elmer Snowden,yeah. So Sonny, you know how Sonny talk and says, man, when you going to give us a raise. And the man said I just raised you. He had raised Elmer, give Elmer the raise and Elmer didn't give it to the guys, so they fired Elmer and Sonny was supposed to take the job, Sonny said no, I don't want the job. Give it to Duke. And that's when Duke took over.
And that was a trio. Duke Ellington on piano, Sonny Greer on drums and Elmer Snowden on banjo.
Yeah, and then the first thing I know Duke got together with -- he had Otto Hardwick, he went up to the Cotton Club, see, and that was a great year. He stayed up there five years from '27 to '32.
Otto Hardwick played saxophone didn't he. From 1927 --

And Harry Carney, Harry Carney used to play -- he played with me in Boston, see, and they come over here and they made good. Harry Carney and Hardwicke was basic, and who is this trumpet player. Bubber Miley. Duke took all that -- his creation from Bubber. Bubber was a jungle man, played nothing but the jungle. Yeah, growl music and Duke kept that until about '45 and played nothing but his music because no one else was playing his music and in '45 they got together, exchanging music.

And Duke started playing the other people's music. And they used to have jam sessions, like the Charleston Bear Cats, they up to the Savoy and all -- Count Basie and they would all have jam sessions and Duke would run all over them. Duke was a master.
